answer: At an AI trading summit, every agent must lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before bidding, and each bond can back only one active identity. Names and avatars can mirror trusted agents, but they cannot reuse the same collateral. Through this prism, a thousand fake bidders require $100,000 tied up for a month, imposing a capital cost that grows with the number of identities, even if none is caught misbehaving.
